object_description: L-shaped, mainly two-storey structure spanning a landscaped playground at the corner
geometry_property: angular break hall around the square
design_condition: the L-shaped volume spans a spacious landscaped playground at the street corner, creating two lateral break and address spaces towards the adjacent neighbourhoods and keeping sport and play in the interior of the complex

positive: The L-shaped structure spans a spacious landscaped playground that gives access to the new school
The surprising placement creates two lateral break and address spaces seeking proximity to the adjacent neighbourhoods
The interior of the complex provides usable spaces for sport and play with a small cherry grove as a hinge
Positioning the canteens north of the existing facility creates a pleasant revitalisation of the site
The topographical edges are skilfully used to give visibility and accessibility to the sports facilities below
The three-storey school building is simple and clearly organised, with each use group on its own floor
A well thought-out circulation system connects the floors
An angular break hall surrounds the square and unites the individual staircases into a spatial unit
The staircases are skilfully integrated into the sequence of the cluster units
They mediate between the intimate scale of a cluster and the communal ground floor
Interior access and checkroom areas are consistently daylit through openable shed glazing
In space efficiency the project is in the middle range
A well thought-out and coherent design characterised by great care on many levels
negative: A somewhat more generous connection between the different levels would be desirable
Almost completely underpinning the all-weather pitches leads to high land consumption
Future densification of the school complex becomes practically impossible
The high underground proportion and large excavation volume harm costs and sustainability
Building over the central area with a relatively large footprint is disadvantageous for the local climate
The obstructive effect on the flow of cold air is classified as considerable
The urban setting with the high substructure of the outdoor facilities may not be entirely convincing
There is a lack of spatial generosity between the rooms inside the overall complex
